subject: physics

moments.title: Particle zoo
moments.body: Post-WWII experiments discover dozens of new particles: pions, kaons, lambdas, sigmas. Wolfgang Pauli quips: 'Had I foreseen this, I would have gone into botany.'
moments.takeaway: Discovery outpaces theory. Order is desperately needed.

moments.title: Gell-Mann and Zweig propose quarks
moments.who: Murray Gell-Mann, Caltech; George Zweig, CERN
moments.body: Gell-Mann (who names them 'quarks' from Joyce's Finnegans Wake) and Zweig independently propose hadrons are built from three particles with fractional charge. The theory predicts the omega-minus, which is duly discovered. Zweig's paper is rejected; Gell-Mann wins the 1969 Nobel alone.

quote.attrib: Joyce, Finnegans Wake — source of the name

moments.takeaway: Mathematical patterns predict particles before they are found.

moments.title: Deep inelastic scattering at SLAC
moments.body: At SLAC, high-energy electrons fired at protons bounce off at large angles — exactly as Rutherford's alphas bounced off gold nuclei. The proton has internal structure. Feynman calls the components 'partons'; they are quarks.
moments.takeaway: Rutherford's experiment, at a billion times the energy, reveals the proton's quark structure.

moments.title: Top quark at Fermilab
moments.body: The Tevatron discovers the top quark, completing the standard model's quark sector. Its mass, 173 GeV, is as heavy as a gold atom — astonishing for a fundamental particle.
moments.takeaway: All six quarks confirmed. The standard model is one of the most successful theories in physics history.

now.title: Where we are today
now.body: The standard model has 17 fundamental particles plus the Higgs. The LHC produces top quarks and Higgs bosons routinely. But the SM says nothing about dark matter, dark energy or gravity, and cannot explain neutrino mass.
now.open_questions: Why three generations? Why these mass values? Is there a deeper theory?

reflection: Gell-Mann initially called quarks a 'mathematical fiction'. When does a useful fiction become a real entity?
